headline: Sequencing pipelines validated against defined references or simulated datasets
label: Sequencing Pipeline Benchmarking
summary: Recent preprints and one published method report accuracy-checked pipelines for long-read, metatranscriptomic, rDNA, and plant-DNA sequencing data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking of computational pipelines for sequencing data against defined references or simulated datasets. ITSxRust extracts ITS regions from long-read amplicon data using HMMER with partial-chain recovery and QC diagnostics. rDNAmine is an alignment-free toolkit for long tandem rDNA arrays in Nanopore reads, validated on yeast and Candida albicans rDNA. MetaTracer assigns metatranscriptomic reads to taxa and expressed genes in one nucleotide alignment-based pass. krepp, a published method, places sequencing reads genome-wide on ultra-large reference phylogenies using k-mer maximum pseudo-likelihood. SPrOUT identifies angiosperm taxa in mixed plant DNA using Angiosperms353 target sequencing, HybPiper assembly, and phylogenetic distance cutoffs. The items do not share a single method. What is common is explicit evaluation against known or simulated references, and the long-read-aware or alignment-free design of several tools is the notable new element.
